songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Alligator>Caution climax, tight Dark Star and stellar segues
ai_show_review.blurb: The set rocks with a smoking Alligator → Caution sequence and a tightly executed Dark Star. Highlights include The Eleven, the Cryptical‑>The Other One drum segue and an uplifting Morning Dew encore. Recording quality is good despite occasional tape cuts.
ai_show_review.review: On March 16, 1968 at San Francisco’s Carousel Ballroom, the Dead turned in a high‑energy performance that still feels fresh. Set 1 opens with a focused Dark Star that flows into a bright China Cat Sunflower before collapsing into the rhythmic surge of The Eleven and a soulful rendition of Good Morning Little School Girl. After a brief It Hurts Me Too, the band launches into an extended Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One suite, highlighted by Mickey Hart’s seamless drum segue that keeps the momentum alive despite a few tape glitches. The second set builds to a thunderous Alligator → Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) climax, punctuated with wild Feedback and a gentle Good Night send‑off, while the encore Morning Dew showcases Jerry’s soaring lead work and Phil’s dancing bass lines. Both Miller soundboard captures preserve the era’s raw ambience; the Miller SBD (gd1968-03-16.sbd.miller.109944.flac16) stands out for its clearer image and fewer drops, making it the preferred listen.

best_recording.reason: Clearer soundboard with fewer tape cuts; captures the full Alligator → Caution sequence and drum segue in a single track.

key_highlights: Smoking Alligator → Caution climax with Feedback
Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One drum segue
Strong performances of The Eleven, China Cat Sunflower and Morning Dew

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers soaring lead work, especially the “mountain jam” licks in Alligator and fiery phrasing toward the end of The Eleven; a minor stumble is noted at the start of China Cat.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass sounds heavy‑muddy at times but shines on The Eleven and dances with Jerry during Morning Dew, providing a solid low‑end foundation throughout.
band_performance.Ron \"Pigpen\" McKernan: Pigpen adds characteristic harp‑bottle texture and strong vocal presence on Good Morning Little School Girl, enhancing the early set’s blues feel.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart crafts an impressive drum segue between Cryptical Envelopment and The Other One, keeping the flow tight despite tape imperfections.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann supplies steady, propulsive drumming that underpins the extended jams, though no specific moments are singled out in the reviews.

must_listen_sequences: And We Bid You Good Night
